name: onionprobe
desc: Test and monitoring tool for Tor Onion Services
why: Probing Tor onion services is a window into how hidden services are published and reachable, though it is mostly a monitoring tool.

brief.what_it_is: Onionprobe is a command-line tool, installed as the executable `onionprobe`, that tests and monitors the reachability of Tor Onion Services sites. It can run once or continuously, probing a set of onion service endpoints and paths. Per the homepage it can optionally export results to Prometheus, with Grafana and Alertmanager support. The homepage and features page do not spell out the exact inputs and outputs beyond this.
brief.why_it_exists: The features page frames it as a way to measure onion services from the outside, so a user sees what a real visitor sees. It is meant for monitoring any public onion service, not only one's own, and for large infrastructures or researchers collecting public data on reachability.
brief.how_it_works: The features page says Onionprobe runs from anywhere that can reach the Tor network, so it does not need to run alongside the services. It measures effective latency and intermittent failures a user would experience, and does not collect server-side data like the Tor daemon's MetricsPort. The features page also says a standalone node comes with everything needed to test, measure and visualize, and that advanced operators can run just the core service or use it as a library.
brief.install_notes: Not found. The homepage and features page do not give install steps. The features page points to an 'installation options' page, but the URL I guessed for it returned 404. The brew formula's executable is `onionprobe`. Nothing I read mentions hardware, accounts, runtimes or first-run configuration.
brief.standout: Probing from outside the operator's network, through the Tor network, measures what a user actually experiences of an onion service, rather than the server's own internal metrics. It is also built to feed Prometheus, Grafana and Alertmanager, so it fits into standard monitoring stacks.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage and features page show no release dates, version numbers or commit dates. The GitLab repository returned HTTP 403, so I could not check its activity.
brief.caveats: The GitLab repository and the installation docs were not readable, so I could not confirm the command-line interface, supported platforms, licence or build requirements. The features page says probing needs the Tor network to be reachable. The brew formula has no caveats.
quotes: Onionprobe is a tool for testing and monitoring the status of Tor Onion Services sites.
It can run a single time or continuously to probe a set of onion services endpoints and paths, optionally exporting to Prometheus and with Grafana and Alertmanager support.
Onionprobe's collected data better represents the actual user experience in terms of Onion Service reachability and performance.
